text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock has fallen about 2% over the past week, sliding from $478 down to $457 today, despite oil prices climbing to six-month highs above $116 a barrel. The weakness comes even as refinery utilization sits at a healthy 93.4%, suggesting the move isn't about operational challenges. Instead, the stock appears to be caught in a reversal of the geopolitical risk premium that initially pushed energy stocks higher—as Middle East tensions (Houthi attacks, U.S.-Iran frictions) have persisted without escalating dramatically further, some of those gains are being trimmed back.

The broader pattern here is that refiners benefit from higher oil prices in a specific way: they profit from the spread between crude costs and finished fuel prices. Right now, storage levels for gasoline and diesel are historically normal, so refiners can't simply pocket the full benefit of $107–115 oil. With the initial shock of geopolitical risk already priced in and no fresh operational catalyst, the stock is drifting lower alongside a normalization of what initially looked like a short, sharp rally.
